title: Surjectivity and boundary kernel of Picard restriction
statement: Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ [def-sc-curves], and let $c:C\hookrightarrow Z$ be a compactification [lem-sc-compactification] with $Z$ a smooth connected curve. Pullback of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] gives a surjective homomorphism $r:\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ [def-sc-picard-group], and $\ker r=\langle[\mathcal O_Z(P)]:P\text{ a closed point of }Z\setminus C\rangle$. No degree-zero quotient or choice of boundary point is asserted.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: Install both k-scheme structures. Smoothness gives regularity, and connected regular schemes are integral; finite type gives Noetherianity. The dimension-one hypothesis on C gives smooth relative dimension one. Use the existing point-ideal divisor-class equivalence and quotient surjectivity to deduce that Divisor.toPic is surjective on both schemes.

For a class L on C choose a divisor D representing it. Induct on D using Finsupp.induction_linear. The zero divisor lifts to 1; sums lift by multiplying lifts; a single n[Q] lifts to the nth power of the class O(P) furnished by the point-lift lemma. This proves Picard restriction is surjective.

Let B be the subgroup closure of the boundary-point classes. For a kernel class L choose an ambient divisor D using divisor-class surjectivity. Apply principal correction to get a divisor E with the same Picard class and zero coefficients on C. Rewrite E as its finite sum of point divisors. Every supporting point lies outside C, so each O(P) lies in B; closure under integer powers and finite products gives L in B.
For the reverse inclusion apply Subgroup.closure_le. Every boundary generator maps to 1 by boundary triviality, hence belongs to the kernel. Antisymmetry gives the claimed subgroup equality.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_exact
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g]
    [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] :
    Function.Surjective (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i) ∧
      (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i).ker = Subgroup.closure
        {L | ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧
          L = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P}
